claim.pdf_says: The three clause lines printed as plain (non-boxed) format lines carry selective underlining: `ACCESS` and `SEQUENTIAL` are underlined while MODE and IS are not; `STATUS` is underlined while FILE and IS are not; `ORGANIZATION` and `SEQUENTIAL` are underlined while IS is not; `SELECT` and `OPTIONAL` are underlined.
claim.markdown_says: ISO_COBOL.md renders these with no underline markup and no compensating figure note - e.g. line 14835 `[ ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL ]`, and likewise `[ FILE STATUS IS data-name-4 ]`, `SELECT [ OPTIONAL ] file-name-1`, `[ [ ORGANIZATION IS ] SEQUENTIAL ] .` in the same page-344 slice.
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining is the standard's only marker separating required words from optional words (5.2.6.2). With it gone and no figure note to carry it, MODE, IS and FILE read as required, so legal source such as `ACCESS SEQUENTIAL` or `STATUS IS data-name-4` looks illegal. Elsewhere the transcription does preserve this - page 310 uses `<u>PROGRAM-ID</u>`, page 322 uses `<u>SYMBOLIC</u> CHARACTERS`, and every code-block figure on page 344 itself carries a figure note listing the underlined words - so these plain lines are an omission rather than a convention.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed independently at glyph level from a 300dpi render of spec_p344.png, with the page-344 slice (ISO_COBOL.md lines 14816-14898) read directly. I tried to refute this four ways and it survived all four. (1) IS THE UNDERLINE REALLY PRINTED? Yes. I cropped and upscaled each line 2.2x and read the glyphs myself. `SELECT [ OPTIONAL ] file-name-1`: a rule runs under SELECT and under OPTIONAL; file-name-1 and the brackets are clean. `[ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL]`: a rule under ACCESS, a rule under SEQUENTIAL, nothing under MODE or IS. `[FILE STATUS IS data-name-4]`: a rule under STATUS only - FILE is clean, IS is clean, data-name-4 is clean. `[ [ORGANIZATION IS] SEQUENTIAL ]` (Format 4): a rule under ORGANIZATION and a rule under SEQUENTIAL, nothing under IS. Every per-word assertion in the claim matches what is printed. (2) IS THE INFORMATION PRESENT SOMEWHERE ELSE ON THE PAGE - reflowed, on an adjacent line, or in a note? No. The page-344 slice has exactly seven fenced code blocks (ASSIGN F3, LOCK MODE, ORGANIZATION F3, RECORD DELIMITER, RESERVE, SHARING, ASSIGN F4) and every one of the seven is followed by a `> **Figure notes ...**` paragraph naming its underlined words. Five lines sit OUTSIDE any fence - slice lines 8 and 65 (`SELECT [ OPTIONAL ] file-name-1`, twice), 20 (`[ ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL ]`), 22 (`[ FILE STATUS IS data-name-4 ]`) and 77 (`[ [ ORGANIZATION IS ] SEQUENTIAL ] .`). None of the five carries `` markup and none is covered by any note. I also checked the tail of the page-343 slice for a carry-over note that might span the page break: page 343's note is explicitly scoped ('Figure notes (SELECT statement Format 2 (relative) syntax diagram)') and ends before the `` anchor. Nothing carries the data forward. (3) IS THIS MERELY FORMATTING / A HOUSE CONVENTION OF THE TRANSCRIPTION? No - it contradicts the transcription's own established convention, and the proof is one page earlier. ISO_COBOL.md line 14784 (page 343) renders the IDENTICAL line as `SELECT [ OPTIONAL ] file-name-1`, and line 15269 renders the identical clause as `FILE STATUS IS data-name-1` - FILE bare, STATUS underlined, exactly matching the glyphs I read on page 344. The file uses `` markup in 97 places overall, and the claim's two corroborating examples check out: `PROGRAM-ID` is at line 13552, inside the page-310 slice (anchors 13521..13577), and `SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS` is at line 14016, inside the page-322 slice (anchors 14009..14057). So page 344's bare lines are an omission, not a policy. (4) DOES IT CHANGE MEANING? Yes. 5.2.2 Keywords: keywords 'are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword.' 5.2.3 Optional words: optional words 'are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity.' Underlining is the sole discriminator. Stripped of it, a reader or a tool consuming ISO_COBOL.md sees MODE, IS and FILE as required, so `ACCESS SEQUENTIAL`, `LOCK MODE IS ...` written as `ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL`, and `STATUS IS data-name-4` all read as illegal when the standard permits them, while conversely nothing marks ACCESS/STATUS/ORGANIZATION/SELECT/OPTIONAL/SEQUENTIAL as the words that may not be dropped. Mitigation worth recording: the same clauses have their own normative general formats later (12.4.5.4 ACCESS MODE p319, 12.4.5.8 FILE STATUS p324, 12.4.5.10 ORGANIZATION p327), so the required/optional split is recoverable from the document as a whole. That bounds the blast radius but does not make the page-344 transcription faithful.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, with three corrections to the claim as written.

(a) COUNT: it is not 'three clause lines'. Five physical lines in the page-344 slice are affected, covering four distinct clause patterns - `SELECT [ OPTIONAL ] file-name-1` appears TWICE (slice line 8 under 'Format 3 (sequential):' and slice line 65 under 'Format 4 (sort-merge):', i.e. ISO_COBOL.md lines 14823 and 14880), plus `[ ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL ]` (14835), `[ FILE STATUS IS data-name-4 ]` (14837) and `[ [ ORGANIZATION IS ] SEQUENTIAL ] .` (14892).

(b) CITATION: the underlining convention is 5.2.2 (Keywords) and 5.2.3 (Optional words), not '5.2.6.2'. 5.2.6 is 'Options', which governs the bracket/brace meta-language, a different convention. The claim's rationale is right but points at the wrong section.

(c) SCOPE OF THE ORGANIZATION ITEM: only the FORMAT 4 ORGANIZATION line (`[ [ ORGANIZATION IS ] SEQUENTIAL ] .`) is affected. Format 3's ORGANIZATION clause is inside a fenced block and IS correctly covered by its figure note, which already states that ORGANIZATION, LINE and SEQUENTIAL are underlined and RECORD and IS are not.

Exact underlining to restore, read off the 300dpi render:
  - `<u>SELECT</u> [ <u>OPTIONAL</u> ] file-name-1`  (both occurrences; file-name-1 bare)
  - `[ <u>ACCESS</u> MODE IS <u>SEQUENTIAL</u> ]`
  - `[ FILE <u>STATUS</u> IS data-name-4 ]`  (FILE deliberately NOT underlined)
  - `[ [ <u>ORGANIZATION</u> IS ] <u>SEQUENTIAL</u> ] .`
This matches byte-for-byte how ISO_COBOL.md already renders the same two constructs at lines 14784 and 15269.

Severity is understated as 'cosmetic'. Underlining is semantic in this document - it is the only marker of required vs optional words - so this is a content-fidelity defect that inverts the required/optional status of MODE, IS and FILE for any consumer of the markdown. Recommend re-classifying to minor/substantive. The fix is mechanical: add the `<u>` markup to the five lines, matching the convention already used on the neighbouring pages; no figure note is needed since these are single plain lines rather than fenced diagrams.
